50961222.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human thymus flag-tagged full-length FANCF expressed in HEK293T cells assessed as dissociation constant by surface plasmon resonance assay

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Surface plasmon: The binding kinetics of DOX and the FANCF protein were analyzed using the Biacore 3000 instrument (GE Healthcare). DOX was immobilized onto a sensor chip CM5, typically between 10 and 50 RU, using an amine coupling kit (GE Healthcare). Different concentrations of the FANCF protein in PBS-T were injected for 120 s at a flow rate of 20 μL/min. BIAevaluation 4.1 software was used to determine the kinetic parameters. The binding between DOX and BSA (Wako, Osaka, Japan) was analyzed in the same manner.
original_paragraph.Results - 2.3.2. Surface plasmon resonan: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) analysis was carried out to determine kinetic parameters of the DOX-FANCF interaction. DOX itself was immobilized on a sensor chip of an SPR biosensor (Biacore 3000) and then tested against various concentrations of recombinant FANCF protein. Our results showed that the binding between DOX and FANCF occurred in a dose-dependent manner (Fig. 3B, Table 3). The dissociation constant (Kd) of direct interaction between DOX and FANCF was determined to be 5.3 × 10−7 M, which is a relatively high affinity. Bovine serum albumin (BSA) as a negative control did not represent any binding against DOX in the same range of concentrations as that for calculation of the dissociation constant between FANCF and DOX (Supplementary Fig. 2).
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Figure 3. Binding analysis of recombinant FANCF with DOX. (A) Detection of FANCF binding to DOX by pull-down assay. Cell extracts of HEK293T cells overexpressing flag-FANCF were prepared and used for the assay. Proteins bound to DOX-Bio-immobilized avidin agarose resins were isolated and detected by Western blot analysis using anti-FANCF antibody (lane: DOX-Bio). As a control, proteins bound to avidin agarose resins were detected (lane: only resins). (B) An SPR analysis for the binding between DOX and FANCF. Analytes were injected over flow cells on the immobilized DOX. The background resulting from an injection of running buffer was subtracted from the data before plotting. Resonance units (RU) were generated by subtraction of the background signal generated simultaneously on the control flow cell.
original_paragraph.Table 3: Table 3 Summary of kinetic parameters of the interaction between DOX and FANCF calculated by BIAevaluation 4.1 software. ka: association rate constant, kd: dissociation rate constant, KA: association constant, Kd: dissociation constant ka (M−1 s−1) 6.5 × 103 kd (s−1) 1.8 × 10−3 KA (M−1) 5.2 × 106 Kd (M) 5.3 × 10−7
original_paragraph.Figure 3B plot description: Figure 3B shows a sensorgram with the x-axis labeled 'Time (sec)' ranging from -100 to 300 seconds and the y-axis labeled 'Response (RU)' ranging from -20 to 60. The plot contains five curves, each corresponding to a different final concentration of FANCF (μM): 1.25, 0.625, 0.313, 0.156, and 0.0781. The curves show an initial increase in response (association phase) followed by a decrease (dissociation phase).
